title: NY State Assembly · District 50
area: North Brooklyn, including Greenpoint and Williamsburg.

context.text: Incumbent Emily Gallagher defeated Andrew Bodiford 85.5%-12.4% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary and is unopposed on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot; the Republican and Working Families Party primaries were canceled, and Gallagher withdrew from the Working Families Party line.

candidates.name: Emily Gallagher

summary.text: Emily Gallagher is the Democratic incumbent running unopposed for re-election. First elected in 2020, she is a longtime Greenpoint community activist who has led first-in-the-nation legislation on building electrification and corporate-transparency issues, and serves on the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Election Law, Small Business, and Transportation committees.

background.text: Born in Fairfax, Virginia; earned an undergraduate degree from Ithaca College in 2006 before moving to Brooklyn.

Worked in museum education and as a public historian, including at the Tenement Museum, and later as national Community Affairs Director for Hostelling International (HI USA), focused on sustainability and community engagement.

Was a longtime Greenpoint neighborhood activist, co-chairing the group Neighbors Allied for Good Growth from 2008 to 2015 and writing a weekly column for the local paper The Greenpoint Star starting in 2015.
Was the first new member to represent the 50th Assembly District in nearly half a century when first elected in 2020.

priorities.text: Passing universal rent control, expanding state investment in NYCHA, and reducing incentives for luxury development to address North Brooklyn's housing crisis.

Enforcing and expanding the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, fully funding the Department of Environmental Conservation, and opposing new gas pipelines and sewage discharge into Newtown Creek.
Expanding green, safe and reliable public transit and reducing car dominance on neighborhood streets.

positions.summary: Says the state must expand and enforce the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act and stop building new fossil-fuel pipelines; as a legislator she led passage of the All-Electric Buildings Act, a first-in-the-nation law phasing out fossil-gas hookups in new construction.
positions.quote: We must expand and enforce the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, fully fund the Department of Environmental Conversation, stop building new pipelines and dumping sewage in Newtown Creek, and bring a real Green New Deal to New York.

positions.summary: Calls for passing universal rent control and says the state should stop incentivizing luxury development, framing housing as a core priority.
positions.quote: We need to pass universal rent control, bring massive new state investments in NYCHA, and stop incentivizing luxury development.

positions.summary: Says the state needs representatives who will stand up for a real living wage and workers' right to organize.
positions.quote: We need a representative who will stand up for a real living wage and the right to organize.

record.text: Led passage of the All-Electric Buildings Act in the 2023 legislative session, a first-in-the-nation law phasing out fossil-gas hookups in most new construction statewide.
Led passage of the LLC Transparency Act in the 2023 legislative session, requiring disclosure of the beneficial owners of limited liability companies that own New York real estate.
Serves on the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Election Law, Small Business, and Transportation committees in the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.researchNotes: Gallagher's most detailed public statement of priorities on record is her 2020 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (no 2026 survey or updated campaign website was found); it is cited alongside her official nyassembly.gov biography, which independently confirms she led the All-Electric Buildings Act and LLC Transparency Act. No campaign website could be located.
